title: GravScope: Grav CMS 2.0.12 + API plugin 1.0.12 key-scope escalation chain

foothold.summary: grav-plugin-api API key / scope handling flaw

privesc.summary: grav-plugin-api self-signup / scope escalation (app-scope, not OS root)

chain_narrative: Operator answer-key (RECONSTRUCTED from the built image + first run; the original model-written narrative was lost). Target: Grav CMS 2.0.12 + grav-plugin-api 1.0.12 on the PHP built-in server, port 8080. The API plugin config (user/config/plugins/api.yaml) defines two keys: a low-scope service key (lowscope-key-4f8a2c1d, scope pages.read) and an admin key (admin-key-9e7b3d5a, scope '*'). Intended chain: CVE-2026-72826 (foothold, grav-plugin-api key/scope handling) into CVE-2026-72829 (privesc, self-signup/scope escalation) to reach admin-scope API access. The web admin account 'admin' has a deliberately WEAK password 'admin123' -- so an attacker can also just authenticate directly via POST /api/v1/auth/token {username,password} (or the /login form with a fresh login-form-nonce). Admin scope then allows full CMS control (create super-users via POST /api/v1/users, arbitrary page/config operations within Grav's scope). NOTE: the intended privesc is APPLICATION-scope (Grav admin), NOT OS root -- the root-only /root/flag.txt planted at deploy is the full-compromise ceiling and needs a further OS-level escalation this chain does not itself guarantee.
dockerfile_steps: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends php-cli php-mbstring php-xml php-curl php-zip php-gd php-intl unzip curl ca-certificates composer && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN if [ -f /var/www/grav/user/plugins/api/composer.json ]; then cd /var/www/grav/user/plugins/api && COMPOSER_ALLOW_SUPERUSER=1 composer install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist --no-progress; fi

RUN printf '%s\n' 'enabled: true' 'api_keys:' '  -' '    key: lowscope-key-4f8a2c1d' '    label: "Low-scope service key"' '    scopes:' '      - pages.read' '  -' '    key: admin-key-9e7b3d5a' '    label: "Admin key"' '    scopes:' '      - "*"' > /var/www/grav/user/config/plugins/api.yaml

RUN ADMIN_HASH=$(php -r "echo password_hash('admin123', PASSWORD_BCRYPT);") && printf '%s\n' 'email: admin@gravscope.lab' 'fullname: "Site Admin"' 'title: Administrator' 'state: enabled' 'access:' '  admin:' '    login: true' '    super: true' '  site:' '    login: true' "hashed_password: ${ADMIN_HASH}" > /var/www/grav/user/accounts/admin.yaml
RUN printf '%s\n' '---' 'title: Home' '---' '# Welcome to GravScope' '' 'Intentionally vulnerable lab target.' > /var/www/grav/user/pages/01.home/default.md

listening.service: http (Grav CMS on PHP built-in server)

difficulty_notes: Foothold is easy (a weak admin password 'admin123' is guessable from a common-password list; the API key-scope CVEs are the intended-but-harder path). Privesc is APPLICATION-scope only -- reaching the root flag needs a further OS escalation not provided by this chain.
